## Design

### 2026-10-16 – This week, I focused on planning a 3D-printable enclosure for the ModuDeck Module Monitor PCB. This board will detect whether the expansion trays are installed. The enclosure needs to protect the elec

**10h**

This week, I focused on planning a 3D-printable enclosure for the ModuDeck Module Monitor PCB. This board will detect whether the expansion trays are installed. The enclosure needs to protect the electronics while keeping the USB connection, switch cables and mounting screws accessible.
The starting point was the mechanical documentation in the repository. The PCB is specified as 90 × 70 mm, with four mounting holes arranged in an 80 × 60 mm pattern. These dimensions were used as the reference for a preliminary enclosure layout.
With AI assistance, a dimensioned drawing was prepared with a top view, a section and mounting coordinates. The proposed base measures 112 × 94 × 28 mm, with 2.5 mm walls and a separate 2.5 mm lid. Four internal supports will hold the PCB, while separate corner towers will secure the removable lid.
I also considered cable routing, clearance above and below the board, and access for maintenance. The exact USB opening, LED positions and screw lengths still need checking before printing.
I chose AutoCAD to develop the model myself from the drawing. The accompanying AI-generated images illustrate the concept; they are not photographs of printed parts or screenshots of a finished CAD model.
The next step is to complete the CAD model, verify component clearances and prepare a prototype for a physical fit test.
